title: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM)
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 1: Security and Risk Management: Supply Chain Risk Management (SCRM).

items: Assess and manage risks from third-party vendors and suppliers
Evaluate vendor security practices before engagement
Include security requirements in contracts and SLAs
Monitor vendor compliance throughout the relationship
Apply minimum security baselines to all third parties
NIST SP 800-161 — Supply Chain Risk Management Practices for Federal Information Systems [VERIFY — specific 800-161 content not in RAG]
Hardware Root of Trust — verify hardware integrity from manufacturing to deployment; prevents supply chain tampering (e.g., implanted backdoors in chips or firmware)

blocks.text: Supply chain risk is increasingly important as organizations depend on third-party services, cloud providers, and global supply chains. Key SCRM activities:

items: Vendor Assessment — Evaluate security posture before engagement (questionnaires, SOC 2 reports, ISO 27001 certification, penetration test results)
Contract Requirements — Include security requirements, right-to-audit clauses, breach notification, data handling obligations
SLA Monitoring — Verify vendor meets security requirements through continuous assessment
Fourth-Party Risk — Consider the vendors your vendors use (your cloud provider's subcontractors)
Hardware/Software Integrity — Verify supply chain integrity to prevent tampering

rows: Independent audit of controls over time
Contractual right to audit vendor directly

blocks.text: Hardware Root of Trust ensures that hardware components have not been tampered with during manufacturing or transit. This includes:

items: Trusted Platform Module (TPM) — hardware chip that provides cryptographic functions and secure boot verification
Supply chain validation — verifying the provenance of hardware from manufacturer to deployment
Firmware integrity checking — ensuring firmware has not been modified with malicious code
Bill of Materials (BOM) verification — confirming components match specifications

blocks.text: From Destination CISSP: "When working with an external service, be sure to review any SLA (service-level agreements) to ensure that the security requirements for new hardware, software, or services should always meet or exceed the security of your existing infrastructure." ⚠️ Exam Trap: SCRM is not just about evaluating vendors at the start — it requires CONTINUOUS monitoring throughout the relationship. The exam expects a manager mindset: establish requirements in contracts, verify through audits, and maintain ongoing oversight. Hardware root of trust prevents supply chain attacks at the physical level.
